funding.name: AAS South Asia Council Dissertation Workshop Grant
funding.amount_note: Covers lowest economy-class airfare from home location to Shanghai, AAS-in-Asia 2027 conference registration fee, shared-room lodging during the workshop, and meals during the workshop
funding.requires: Selection as one of 10 workshop participants; full application (incl. advisor recommendation letter) by the deadline
funding.why: Open to advanced doctoral candidates on South Asia dissertations with priority to Asia-based applicants, which favors her (Hyderabad-based); however she is a 2nd-year PhD student, and the call specifies candidates who have completed their research and are writing their dissertation, which she may not yet meet
funding.source_quote: Students selected for the workshop will receive a grant to cover the costs of: Lowest economy-class airfare from their home location to Shanghai
funding.sequence_note: The 2026 window (deadline 30 May 2026) has closed. Watch for a 2027 call with a similar cycle, and apply once her dissertation research is far enough along to meet the 'advanced candidate' bar.

registration.note: No separate registration fee for the workshop; would be covered by the grant if selected

travel.note: If selected, the grant covers lowest economy-class airfare from home location to Shanghai

accommodation.note: If selected, the grant covers shared-room lodging and meals during the workshop

visa.note: China single-entry visa fee (~₹2,900) plus visa application service center charge (~₹2,100); not mentioned as covered by the workshop grant
visa.source: Chinese Visa Application Service Center (New Delhi) fee table, checked Aug 2026

assumptions: Assumes selection into the workshop; if selected, the AAS grant covers airfare, registration, shared lodging, and meals per the call text
Visa cost is the only expense not explicitly covered by the grant

No FX conversion needed — visa fee is already quoted in INR
cost_estimate.net_note: If selected for a future cycle, this trip would cost close to nothing beyond the China visa fee (~₹5,000–5,500), since the grant covers airfare, registration, lodging, and meals.

fit.reason: It's a dissertation workshop explicitly for advanced doctoral candidates writing South Asia dissertations, open across disciplines including media studies and anthropology — a direct match for her Dalit/Bahujan digital-counterpublics dissertation.

standing.reason: No standing_signals were extracted, but the host (AAS South Asia Council) and funder (Henry Luce Foundation) are both well-recognized names in Asian studies — a credible but not independently verified signal.

network.reason: Limited to 10 participants with a virtual pre-meeting and in-person sessions — the kind of small cohort and sustained contact that scores high by nature for a PhD seeking mentoring.

outcomes.reason: Structured dissertation feedback before chapter-writing is exactly her stated goal ('feedback before I write my chapters'), making this the closest outcomes match in her set.

feasibility.reason: The grant covers airfare, registration, lodging and meals if selected, and October is within her available months, but she'd still need a China visa (against her 'prefer no visa' preference), and — most importantly — the 2026 window (deadline 30 May 2026) is already closed with the 2027 cycle not yet announced.

fit.rationale: This is a dissertation workshop explicitly for advanced doctoral candidates writing South Asia-focused dissertations, open across disciplines including media studies and anthropology — precisely the kind of structured, small-group feedback her Dalit/Bahujan digital-counterpublics dissertation would benefit from before she writes her chapters. Priority for Asia-based applicants also favors her Hyderabad affiliation.

why_go: This is built exactly for what you want: structured, small-group feedback on a South Asia dissertation before you write your chapters.
If selected, the grant covers airfare, registration, shared lodging, and meals — only the China visa would be out of pocket.
watch_out: Applications for this cycle closed on 30 May 2026, and it's meant for 'advanced' candidates who've finished their research — as a 2nd-year PhD student, you may not yet qualify; watch for the 2027 call.
Only 10 participants are selected, so it's competitive even once a new cycle opens.
tagline: The feedback workshop you want — but the 2026 door is shut; prepare for the next one.
eligibility_notes: Restricted to advanced doctoral candidates who have completed their research and are writing their dissertation, selected from a pool of applicants (10 spots) with priority to Asia-based candidates (she qualifies on this point as Hyderabad-based). As a 2nd-year PhD student she may not yet meet the 'advanced' bar, and the 2026 window has already closed — eligibility is conditional on a future cycle and her research progress by then.

visa.note: Indian passport holders need a visa to travel to China (via Shanghai). This is general information, not immigration advice — confirm current requirements with the Chinese Embassy/Consulate or the Chinese Visa Application Service Center in India before planning travel.
